summary: Create a Run and bind it as this profile's current Run
usage: corral orchestration run-create [--objective VALUE] [--request-id VALUE] [--help] [--json] [--timeout-ms VALUE] [--socket VALUE] [--instance VALUE]
notes: Records are Run (run_<12 hex>), Task (task_<12 hex>) and Dispatch (ctx_<12 hex>), stored as one JSON document under <userData>/runtime/orchestration/state.json. One mutation is one atomic rename, so a task, its attempt and any dependents promoted by the same call commit together or not at all. Durability is the profile's existing promise: process-crash safe, not power-loss safe (no directory fsync, no F_FULLFSYNC).

The current Run is bound per profile, not per calling terminal. --run <id> overrides it for one call without rebinding it. With neither, commands that need a Run fail run_required before any effect, and resources.recovery names run-create/run-use.

Task status is pending|ready|dispatched|completed|failed|blocked; Dispatch status is dispatched|completed|failed|unknown. failed means an observed failure only: an absent pane, a replaced PTY, a changed backend generation and an unreachable backend are never turned into failed, and nothing is retried automatically.

Every mutation accepts --request-id r1.<13-digit Unix milliseconds>.<UUID> and mints one when it is omitted, sharing the profile's existing 24-hour receipt store. A replayed id returns the first result with replayed true, the same id with different input is request_conflict, and a receipt that is still pending is outcome_unknown and is never re-executed.
This command group starts nothing and sends nothing to any pane. Dispatch records which pane an attempt is bound to; launching the worker, its messages and its completion are LIFE-410.
run-create always rebinds the current Run to the Run it created.

Reconcile re-observes every open attempt before each orchestration command and again on dispatch-show: the same generation alive keeps the attempt dispatched and reports terminal.live true; an absent pane, a replaced PTY or a changed backend generation settles it unknown with reason pane_gone|pty_replaced|epoch_changed and leaves the Task dispatched so it can be dispatched again; an unreachable backend records nothing at all and reports observed false with terminal.live unknown. Only reconcile creates unknown, and it never creates failed.

summary: Transition a Task and settle its open attempt in one atomic write
usage: corral orchestration task-update [--id VALUE] [--status VALUE] [--result VALUE] [--dispatch VALUE] [--expected-version VALUE] [--run VALUE] [--request-id VALUE] [--help] [--json] [--timeout-ms VALUE] [--socket VALUE] [--instance VALUE]
examples: corral orchestration task-update --id task_0a1b2c3d4e5f --status failed --dispatch ctx_0a1b2c3d4e5f --expected-version 3 --json

The manual table is dispatched -> completed|failed, anything except completed -> blocked, and blocked -> ready|pending. ready -> dispatched belongs to the dispatch command alone, and completed is terminal. Anything else is illegal_transition with the allowed set in resources.

Checks run in a fixed order and every rejection is effect-free: --expected-version mismatch is version_conflict, then an illegal transition is illegal_transition, then a --dispatch that is not the open attempt is stale_dispatch. Settling a Task that is already settled is therefore illegal_transition even when the caller names the attempt that settled it, while naming a superseded attempt of a still-open Task is stale_dispatch.

Omitting --dispatch settles whichever attempt is open, which is how a human settles a Task whose attempt reconcile already marked unknown. blocked -> ready additionally requires every dependency completed; blocked -> pending is always available.

summary: Bind a new attempt of a Task to a live terminal handle

notes: Records are Run (run_<12 hex>), Task (task_<12 hex>) and Dispatch (ctx_<12 hex>), stored as one JSON document under <userData>/runtime/orchestration/state.json. --to takes a terminal handle and is resolved by the terminal module's own three-layer check: a handle that does not verify is invalid_terminal, one from another runtime or backend generation or whose PTY is gone or replaced is stale_terminal, and a profile with no reachable backend is backend_unavailable. All three are effect-free.

The attempt stores the target identity (handle, runtimeId, epoch, ptyId, paneId) and a snapshot of the pane's managed agent taken at that moment, or null with agentAbsenceReason when the pane has none. Nothing is sent to the pane and no agent is started.

A Task is startable when it is ready, or when its most recent attempt ended failed or unknown — that retry becomes attempt n+1. An open attempt, a pending Task with unmet dependencies, a blocked Task and a completed Task are all task_not_startable, with reason and unmetDependencies in resources.

The response's terminal block is the observation this call made; the record's reconcile block is the last observation that changed something, with the runtime instance that recorded it. Repeating the call therefore leaves the stored document byte-identical.
